Strategy Audit · snapshot 2026-09-21 17:13

Strategy Test Bench

What is known today about each of the 1356 Freqtrade strategies: which cleared every gate, which did not, and exactly where each one stopped.

Distribution

The order the checks run in

Every stage a strategy passes through, in processing order. Each step needs what the one before it produces, so the order is not arbitrary: look-ahead comes before the warm-up ladder and recursion because recursion refuses to spend a run on a strategy whose look-ahead is not PASS, and a look-ahead finding is not something a warm-up can repair. The counts per stage are the funnel above.

#StageWhat it checksOn failure
0Intaketools/harvest.py Only .py files with an IStrategy subclass are downloaded, with a malware scan, one canonical row per implementation and a duplicate check by hash. A freshly downloaded, still unchecked duplicate is deleted. Once a strategy has been checked, a later duplicate is only excluded (C11), never deleted, because other strategies may import that file.
1Trial runprofile_smoke Does the strategy load and trade? One month over eight pairs, widened to three months and then one year while it has fewer than ten trades. Stays open, never excluded: no check has judged it. What blocks it goes to the repair routes, then the trial run is repeated.
1bRepair routesrepair.controller Missing timeframe, a local module the author shipped beside the file, a changed signature, missing data files. Where no repair would avoid inventing the strategy: C4, C5, C7, C8, C12 or C13.
2Look-aheadprofile_bias Does the strategy see data it could not have had at the time? Runs at the warm-up the author declared, so a strategy that declares none is compared on indicators still undefined at the start of the window; that is recorded on the row. FOUND is a final exclusion (C1). The warm-up ladder and recursion then no longer run.
3Warm-up ladderwarmup_convergence Only after a look-ahead PASS. From which startup (1, 2, 7, 14, 30, 90, 365 days, converted to the strategy's timeframe) do all indicators stay inside 1 percent? No rung converges or the strategy is inconclusive: it is not admitted. The longest rungs failing to run at all is C9.
4Recursionprofile_bias The final check, at the warm-up the ladder settled on. FOUND at every reachable warm-up is C2.
5Data coverage A plain check of the candle files for each pair and window. Gaps are reported. It gives no verdict of its own.
6Mergestrategy_status, pipeline_state Derives each strategy's cohort from all stores. No verdict of its own.
7Admission E1eligibility_admit_converged Clean bias results and a converged warm-up, then back to stage 6 for the cohort. Stays in the queue.
8Full-window backtestregime.full_backtest All eight pairs pooled, 20200301-20260821, hard timeout of 3600 s. The single-pair run counts only for strategies that never trade. No trades over the whole window: C3. Failure, timeout or memory limit: C10. Identical canonical trades to another implementation: C11.
8bExecution robustnessexecution_robustness Above 5m: the same run again with --timeframe-detail 5m, compared with the baseline. At or below 5m: not rerun; owner decision, because such a baseline already simulates at that granularity, so it counts as a passed 5m run. The record says which of the two it is. SENSITIVE (profit changes sign, moves by more than 50 percent, or the trade set moves by more than 10 percent) is a review marker, not an exclusion.
8bCost screenexecution_robustness Does the profit survive an extra 0.1 percent slippage per side, judged separately for each ADX state on the trades that opened in that state, so a specialist strong in one state is not marked down by the others? Validation window from 2024-01-01, at least 10 trades per state. No exclusion. Execution PASS plus cost PASS in at least one state is robustness_qualified: necessary for the label verified specialist, not sufficient.
9Market regime classificationregime_engine Market-level, not per strategy: BTC and coin states from the DMI/ADX model. Computed once and frozen. No verdict.
10Attributionregime.attribution Every trade is assigned by its opening day to the BTC state and to the coin state. No verdict.
11Hypothesis Each strategy's assumed market phase, written before any evaluation looks at results. No verdict.
12Benchmark Models 0 to 3 The original strategy, then the same strategy gated by the BTC state, by the coin state, and by both. Model 0 has run on the measured corpus; Models 1 to 3 have run on the pilot and specialist candidate sets and are partial on the wider ones. No exclusion.
13Specialist and universal evaluation Validation window from 2024-01-01, at least 5 episodes and 10 trades, excess return against an equal-exposure buy-and-hold. The rules are frozen and rankings exist. Only rows above the floor are ranked. The Regime-Spezialisten page adds the stage 8b result to every ranking row; a row with PASS in that column is a verified specialist for its state. The ranking itself does not change.

What excludes a strategy

Thirteen things, and nothing else. Each is a result this audit produced itself, on this data, in this runtime, except C12, which is the owner's recorded decision about scope.

C1 · Look-ahead bias found

freqtrade's lookahead-analysis compared the strategy's signals against a run allowed to see the whole window, and the signals moved. The strategy is reading data it could not have had at the time.

C2 · Recursion bias found by our own ladder

The warm-up ladder climbed every rung the data allows - 1, 2, 7, 14, 30, 90 and 365 days, converted to the strategy's own timeframe - and at each of them at least one indicator still moved by 1.0 % or more against the full-history run. The indicator never settles, so its value depends on where the backtest happens to start.

C3 · Ran the whole window and never traded

The strategy started, ran 20200301-20260821 across all eight pairs, and opened no position at all.

C4 · No repair exists that would not invent the strategy

The strategy declares no timeframe anywhere, no stoploss or an explicit stoploss of 0, no exit logic, no populate_indicators at all, names a prediction model that no longer exists and that this repository holds no copy of, opens a data file (a pre-trained model, a lookup table) the author's own repository never included, or declares two config values in a combination freqtrade refuses (trailing_stop_positive_offset below trailing_stop_positive). A repair route read the file looking for the author's own value and found none to restore, or found two declared values that cannot both be honoured without guessing which one the author meant.

C5 · Local module repair exhausted every candidate

The strategy imports a helper the author shipped beside it in their own repository, and the corpus copy has nowhere to resolve from on its own. repair/local_modules.py searched the whole corpus for another copy that satisfies the import.

C6 · Measured only in the separate FreqAI arm

The strategy is only half a strategy without its FreqAI configuration - the feature set, the model, the training window live in a config file, not the source - and it was measured with the author's own config, in the FreqAI arm's own runtime.

C7 · A missing package with no safe way found to supply it

The strategy imports a package this runtime does not install - sometimes declared by the author, sometimes not, sometimes no longer installable at all.

C8 · The fix would touch every strategy's column writes

Nineteen rows, three known mechanisms, not nineteen bugs. Nine assign a Python bool or int into a column pandas 3.0.5 no longer coerces silently - Invalid value '1' for dtype 'bool' and its mirror images ('True' into float64, a float into int64, an int into str). Eight build a direction column with np.where(cond, np.where(..., 'down', 'up'), np.NaN) - a Supertrend snippet credited to freqtrade/freqtrade-strategies#30, copied near-verbatim into five unrelated repositories - mixing a string branch with a float NaN in one array, which numpy 2.5.2 refuses to promote to a common dtype where older numpy coerced it. The remaining two are each their own break, catalogued individually rather than folded into a count that would overstate how common they are: MomentumRegimeBasket15m compares an int64 column against a datetime64[ms, UTC] one, and MostOfAll loses a computed column outright to pandas copy-on-write - no exception, the column is just not there - which is why it carries no runtime_failure text at all.

C9 · Recursion check cannot complete even at the longest rungs

The ladder's shortest rungs raise inside the strategy's own indicator code rather than reporting a drift table - TRIX_LS (rsi_.rolling(length) on None inside a custom custom_stochRSI helper) and kijun_cross_strong_s (a NoneType subscript). Both already pass a real smoke test on full history, so this is not the strategy failing under real use - it is an indicator that cannot handle the ladder's deliberately extreme short warm-ups. evidence/warmup_convergence.py's resolve() answers that directly: on a crash it drops the shortest rung and retries, continuing until only the 3 longest remain, giving every rung short of those a chance to be the reason before it stops trying. Both rows still crash with only the 3 longest left.

C10 · Canonical pooled full backtest is not testable

The strategy cleared the preceding technical gates, but its canonical all-eight-pairs pooled Stage-7 run did not finish: it failed, exhausted the available resource envelope, or timed out.

C11 · Duplicate implementation with identical canonical trades

The normalized executable source is identical to a retained canonical representative and at least two canonical pooled full backtests have the same trade hash.

C12 · Owner-directed repair scope closure after triage

The owner closed this strategy's repair branch after reviewing the available repair directions, while retaining a smaller, explicitly named set of actionable routes.

C13 · Repeated identical timeout after an exhausted repair route

An author-evidenced compatibility repair was applied, then the same native timeout recurred on a documented retry of that route.

A strategy satisfying none of these is not excluded. It is unfinished, and open_work says what is missing. Five things have at one time or another excluded strategies here and have been withdrawn: the source-code trap heuristic, a verdict inherited from the original sweep, an NA, the analyzer refusing for want of a warm-up, and a failed trial run. Three of them had removed strategies from the work before anyone looked.

The criteria live in exclusion_criteria_list.md and the repair routes in repair_measures_list.md. Both are generated with this page from the same rows, and the generator refuses a row excluded for a reason not written down, or a repair route taken and not recorded.

Windows and pairs

A number cannot be read without knowing what it was measured over. The checks do not share a window, and two of them do not share the pair set either.

The eight pairs against USDT are BTC, ETH, LTC, XRP, ADA, XLM, XMR and DASH, at a 0.1 % fee with max_open_trades=8.

One pair for the bias checks is freqtrade's own doing, not a choice of this audit: recursive-analysis logs “Using pair BTC/USDT only for recursive analysis. Replacing whitelist.” and replaces whatever the config holds.

The look-ahead check widens its window rather than failing. It needs ten trades; when the frozen window yields fewer it retries on the first fallback and then the second, and the record keeps every window it tried. A verdict from a wider window is still that strategy's verdict, but it was not reached over the same span as its neighbour's.

The trial run answers one question: does the strategy start and trade. One month over eight pairs is enough for that and cheap. What it earns is measured later, over the full window.

The warm-up ladder steps in days — 1, 2, 7, 14, 30, 90, 365 — converted to each strategy's own timeframe, and accepts a rung once every indicator stays inside 1.0 %.

Click a column header to sort. A gate reads – when there is no verdict bound to this implementation: either it has not been re-measured, or the only verdict available comes from the original sweep. Hover any cell for the detail.

This is not a softening. Many held rows will end up excluded — the 38 on an inherited look-ahead finding probably will, since a limited environment does not invent bias. They will end up there on our own evidence or not at all.

A plain line was recorded as it ran; one with an amber rule is reconstructed from the run profile and window, because nothing stored the call before 2026-09-01 — a reconstruction is a different claim from a recording. The full-window backtest is eight calls, one per pair; the cell leaves the pair as a placeholder and states the count, while every individual call with its own console output is appended to user_data/freqtrade_runs.log.
